text:
At midday, staff rotas stood out in your long message, and we are sorry you felt let down by the way your companion animal booking was handled and by the delays, mixed messages, and follow-up you received from Aurelia Skyways. The record shows a complaint about poor coordination, slow updates, and concern that the care given to a pet did not match what was promised.

We have reviewed the file against our usual Companion Animal Travel Desk process. Our desk guides passengers through companion animal travel with safety taking priority over speed in every journey. That means the ground team must move carriers carefully between services and keep the care plan aligned with the species, temperament, and comfort needs noted at booking. When this work is done properly, the outcome may not feel quick, but it is meant to protect the animal and reduce handling stress.

In your case, the notes show that the plan needed closer handoff between the booking desk, the ramp team, and the cabin support desk. That is not the standard we expect. Where a passenger is waiting for reassurance, updates should be clear and steady. Where a carrier is being moved, the route should be logged and checked. Where a pet needs a calmer approach, the team should act on that without delay. If that chain breaks, the service feels disjointed, and we understand why you raised the matter.

We are also recording your concern about communication tone. A record aide should keep replies brisk, but not blunt, and the passenger should not be left to chase answers. We have shared your comments with the shift lead so the case can be used in coaching and review. This is part of routine desk work, and it helps us correct gaps before they reach the next traveler.

Please accept our apology for the inconvenience and the added worry this caused. We will keep the file open for service review and will use your report to tighten our handoff checks and response standards.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
